sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the north-western part of West Cape May, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the right. Broadway runs across the middle of the sheet, and the avenues that meet it from the upper side, 1st (the Turnpike), 2nd and 3rd Avenue, are the streets that lead west toward the bay; two unnamed 20 foot lanes run between them. Below Broadway, Myrtle Avenue, York Avenue, Pearl and Emerald Avenue branch off to the east, with West Perry (also called the Turnpike) leaving the sheet at the lower left. The blocks above Broadway are narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings, outbuildings and a wagon house, and one lot at the lower right holds a pigeon house. Hastings and Co. gold leaf factory stands on the block between 2nd Avenue and the next lane. South of Broadway the blocks hold more regular rows of dwellings along York Avenue and Emerald Avenue, with large undivided lots between Myrtle and York Avenues, partly vacant, with a few sheds. A 12 inch water pipe runs along Broadway, with 6 inch pipes in West Perry and Myrtle Avenue. At the bottom of the sheet the tracks of the West Jersey and Sea Shore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) run across the page, with open ground between the tracks and the last houses. A compass rose and the scale bar are drawn in the lower margin, and the sheet is stamped by the Princeton University Library map division.
notes: The Turnpike printed as 1st Avenue and West Perry is Sunset Boulevard and West Perry Street in OpenStreetMap.
Myrtle Avenue is Myrtle Street today; Pearl is Pearl Avenue.
The two unlabelled 20 foot lanes appear in OpenStreetMap as McCullough Alley and Goldbeatten Alley; they were not used as control.
The sheet is turned: Broadway, a north-south street, runs across the page.
Georeferenced from junctions along Broadway only (helmert fit): low confidence for position across the sheet, although the modern street grid overlays the drawn streets well.
West Cape May, turned (north to the right); Broadway, 1st (Turnpike) to 3rd Av, York, Pearl, Emerald, Myrtle, W. Perry; 50 ft; all junctions on Broadway (helmert).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 continues West Cape May to the north of sheet 5, again at 50 feet to an inch and turned with north toward the right. Broadway crosses the sheet from left to right, rising toward the right edge, and meets 4th Avenue and 5th Avenue from the upper side and Emerald Avenue, Eldredge Avenue, Mechanic and Leaming (Columbia) Avenue below. Pacific runs along the top of the sheet, with the 4th Avenue and 5th Avenue blocks between it and Broadway. The upper blocks hold frame dwellings and outbuildings; a Fire Department house with hose carts and a hook and ladder truck stands at the left, pigeon houses lie at the far left edge, and a Presbyterian chapel, heated by furnace and lit by electricity, stands near 5th Avenue. Below Broadway the lots on Emerald Avenue and Eldredge Avenue are small and regular, while Mechanic and Leaming (Columbia) Avenue fan out to the lower right as long diagonal blocks with few buildings. A 12 inch water pipe runs along Broadway. At the bottom left a railroad water tank and a cistern stand beside the West Jersey and Sea Shore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad), and a railroad shed stands beside the tracks near the bottom. The title West Cape May is lettered at the top right.
notes: Leaming (Columbia) Avenue is Leaming Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Pacific is Pacific Avenue; Mechanic is East Mechanic Street.
5th Avenue was not used as control: the OpenStreetMap junction with Broadway lies about 19 m from the drawn one.
The unnamed diagonal street leaving Broadway toward the upper right is 6th Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Georeferenced from 6 junctions with a first-order fit (leave-one-out about 9 m): medium to low confidence.
West Cape May, turned; Broadway, 4th, 5th, Eldredge, Mechanic, Leaming, Pacific; 50 ft; 5th Avenue at Broadway 19 m off its drawn line in OpenStreetMap, not used.

sheet-7-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 7 shows Broadway in West Cape May north of its junction with Leaming Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north slightly to the left of the top of the page. Broadway runs up the page as the road out of town, with numbered frontages on both sides but very few buildings: a handful of frame dwellings and outbuildings stand along it, most of them near the junction at the bottom of the sheet. Leaming Avenue, printed with its alternative name Columbia in brackets, leaves Broadway toward the lower right, lined by small dwellings on narrow lots. At the bottom left a short street with lots numbered 96 to 100 meets Broadway from the west. A 12 inch water pipe from the pumping stations to the north is drawn along Broadway. Block numbers 129, 130 and 131 are printed, and the lower edge joins sheet 6. The large open lots east of Broadway are blank apart from a compass rose. The rest of the page is given to three separate parts divided off by heavy lines: an inset of the Cape May City Water Works new pumping station, the W. L. Stevens and Bro. canning factory with the old water works pumping station beside the railroad, and the West Cape May Public Schools block.
notes: Placed from one measured junction (Broadway / Leaming Avenue) with scale assumed at 7.96 px/ft and rotation from the measured lines; low confidence toward the top of the sheet, where modern Broadway bends to a bearing about 7 degrees east of the drawn line.
Leaming Avenue is printed 'Leaming (Columbia) Av.'; OpenStreetMap has Leaming Avenue.

West Cape May outskirts, 50 ft, four parts: 1 main (Broadway north of Leaming (Columbia) Av), 2 inset of the Cape May City Water Works new pumping station (1 1/2 mile N.W. of city), 3 W. L. Stevens & Bro. canning factory and the water works pumping station on the W.J.&S. R.R. (1 1/4 mile N. of City Hall), 4 West Cape May Public Schools with Columbia, 5th Av and Diamond (now Moore Street). Parts 1 and 4 anchored on one junction each.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Cape May City Water Works new pumping station, 1 1/2 mile N.W. of city (no street or rail feature).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: W. L. Stevens & Bro. canning factory and Cape May City Water Works pumping station on the W.J.&S. R.R., 1 1/4 mile N. of City Hall (no junction: the lane (today Canning House Lane, a stub) no longer reaches the railroad; needs hand-picked point on the railroad plus the lane line; low value).

sheet-7-4.description: Part 4 of sheet 7 is a separate block in the lower right of the page, divided from the main map by a heavy line, showing the West Cape May Public Schools and the streets around them, at 50 feet to an inch. The school building, a two-storey frame structure heated by a furnace and without lights, stands in a long block west of Columbia, marked no exposure on its open sides. East of Columbia, 5th Avenue crosses diagonally at the top with a row of numbered lots, Diamond runs across the middle, and the blocks between and below them are subdivided into numbered lots, nearly all vacant; a single dwelling stands on the block south of Diamond. Lot numbers run along Columbia and both sides of Diamond. Most of the part is open ground.
notes: Diamond is Moore Street in OpenStreetMap: it meets Columbia Avenue at a T and converges with 5th Avenue toward the east as drawn.
Columbia is printed without a suffix (Columbia Avenue today); OpenStreetMap has no junction of Columbia Avenue with 5th Avenue, which the sheet draws.

Placed from one hand-picked junction (Columbia Avenue / Moore Street) and a derived point along Moore Street; scale and rotation assumed (rotation from the modern bearings of Columbia Avenue, Moore Street and 5th Avenue, which agree within 5 degrees; the part's own north arrow disagrees by about 20 degrees). Low confidence.

(1 1/4 mile N. of City Hall), 4 West Cape May Public Schools with Columbia, 5th Av and Diamond (now Moore Street). Parts 1 and 4 anchored on one junction each.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the western end of Cape May City along the ocean front, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the right. Beach Avenue runs down the left side beside the Board Walk and the Atlantic Ocean, Mt. Vernon Avenue runs parallel to it near the right, and 3rd, 2nd and 1st Avenue cross between them, with Broadway at the bottom of the sheet. The blocks are laid out in numbered lots, and most are vacant. Houses stand on the blocks near Beach Avenue, among them a boarding house labelled Villa Nova between 2nd and 3rd Avenue. A pavilion on the Board Walk is cut by the lower left corner. The Cape May, Delaware Bay and Sewells Point Railway Company's power house, with its engine and dynamo room, a water tank and a chimney, stands at the lower right beside the line of the steam and electric railway, which crosses the sheet diagonally from the top toward the lower right. Six inch water pipes run in Beach Avenue and a 12 inch pipe in Broadway. A fire alarm box and several hydrant markers are shown. The street widths are lettered 60 and 70 feet. A compass rose and a scale bar are drawn on the sheet.
notes: Mt. Vernon Avenue is Mount Vernon Avenue; the bottom street printed Broadway is South Broadway in OpenStreetMap.
3rd Avenue does not exist at this place in OpenStreetMap and was not used as control.
The steam and electric railway shown crossing the sheet no longer exists.
West end by the beach, turned; Beach Av, 1st to 3rd Av, Mt. Vernon Av, Broadway (South Broadway today); 50 ft; 3rd Avenue no longer exists here.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 shows the part of Cape May City around the railroad depot, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the right. Broadway forms the top edge, Beach Avenue runs down the left beside the Board Walk and the ocean, and Patterson Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet, with Mt. Vernon Avenue at the right. Two rows of lots between Broadway and Patterson Avenue hold the Sea Crest Inn and several dwellings. South of Patterson Avenue lie more numbered lots and a large open tract carrying the Marine Transmission Company's Wireless Station No. 4. The West Jersey and Sea Shore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) enters from the right as several tracks in a wye and ends at the depot in the lower left, with a long platform and sheds beside the tracks. Cape Island Creek crosses the sheet from the upper right, passes under the railroad and bends toward Grant Street. Grant runs diagonally across the lower right, and North Street and S. Lafayette Street meet it near the bottom. A pavilion on the Board Walk is cut by the left edge. The ocean margin is labelled along the left side.
notes: Mt. Vernon Avenue is Mount Vernon Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the street printed Broadway is South Broadway there; Grant is Grant Street.
The depot, wye and tracks have been removed; the railroad no longer reaches this part of the city.
Georeferenced from 3 detected junctions and 1 carried from sheet 8; the scale fitted is about 2.5 percent above the other sheets: medium to low confidence.
The lower part of the sheet (depot, Grant Street, North Street) has no control of its own.
Patterson Av, Beach Av, Broadway, the railroad depot and wye, Grant, North St, S. Lafayette St; turned; 50 ft; one point carried from sheet-8; the depot area has no control of its own.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers Broadway south of the West Perry turnpike, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies toward the right. Broadway runs across the top, and Grant, Windsor Avenue, Congress and West Perry (the Turnpike) leave it toward the bottom of the sheet. A note at the upper left states that the west side of Broadway is in West Cape May Borough. Cape Island Creek and marsh land lie at the left edge. Along Broadway stand rows of dwellings on narrow lots, and the Neptune Steam Laundry stands on the corner of Congress. The tracks of the West Jersey and Sea Shore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) cross all four streets near the middle of the lower half. Below the tracks stands the American Ice Company's Factory No. 1, with wagon shed, freezing pans, ice house, engine and ice machine and office, and further dwellings fill the lots along the right edge and the angled blocks at the lower left. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches follow the streets, and Myrtle Avenue is lettered at the far right. The scale bar and a compass rose are drawn on the sheet.
notes: The street printed Broadway is South Broadway in OpenStreetMap; Grant is Grant Street, Congress is Congress Street, West Perry is West Perry Street, Myrtle Avenue is Myrtle Street.
The railroad line shown across the lower part of the sheet is gone; its right-of-way is not in the current railway data.
Georeferenced from 4 junctions along Broadway (helmert fit); the modern streets overlay the drawn streets well across the whole sheet: medium confidence.
Broadway south of W. Perry, turned; Grant, Windsor Av, Congress, W. Perry, ice factory; 50 ft; all junctions on Broadway (helmert).

sheet-11-1.description: Sheet 11 covers the western edge of Cape May City, on the west side of town between West Perry Street and Grant Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Cape Island Creek crosses the sheet from top to bottom, shown as a blue channel, and a second branch of the creek crosses Windsor Avenue and Grant Street at the lower left. West of the creek, in the upper left, a row of dwellings fronts West Perry (Turnpike), with a work shop, a wagon shed and large blank lots behind. East of the creek the blocks are filled with two and three storey frame dwellings, boarding houses and hotels. Jackson, Chestnut and Perry converge at the top right, where the blocks along Mansion hold stores and a steam laundry. North Street runs down the middle of the sheet to Windsor Avenue and Grant. Named buildings include Miller Cottage Boarding, the Plaza Boarding, Hotel Devon, the Wyoming, Linden Villa Boarding, the Marcy Boarding, the Mansard and the Wellington (Closed). Six inch water pipes are drawn in the streets and hydrants are marked, with a fire alarm box at Perry. Congress is a wide street crossing the sheet from left to right. Much of the area west of North Street and south of Perry is blank, lot lines only. A boxed area at the lower right, with its own heavy outline, is a separate part drawn on the same sheet. Adjoining sheets are 13, 14, 12, 9 and 10 as numbered on the margins.
notes: West Perry is printed 'W. Perry (Turnpike)'; OpenStreetMap has West Perry Street.
Mansion becomes South Lafayette in the south; OpenStreetMap has Mansion Street and South Lafayette Street as separate names with two nodes about 13 m apart at the Perry junction (both detected).
Chestnut / Mansion was rejected by the fit (10.8 m); modern node is displaced from the drawn corner.

Perry, Jackson, Chestnut, Mansion / S. Lafayette, North, Congress, Windsor Av, Grant; Cape Island Creek; 50 ft; two parts: 1 main, 2 boxed corner at the lower right (Grant / S. Lafayette), placed from one hand-picked point.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is a boxed corner at the lower right of the sheet, outlined with a heavy line, showing the junction of Grant and South Lafayette, drawn at 50 feet to an inch on the same sheet but not contiguous with the main map. It shows the south side of a block holding the Wellington (Closed), a large hotel of two and three storeys, together with a two and a half storey dwelling and outbuildings on lots numbered 27 and 28. South Lafayette runs up the right side of the box, with a ten inch water pipe, a fire alarm box and a hydrant at its corner with Grant, and the block number 12 beyond it names the adjoining sheet. Grant runs along the bottom, with a six inch water pipe; only its north edge is drawn, since the box ends at the sheet margin. A north arrow inside the box points toward the upper left. The block label 11 inside the box repeats the sheet number.
notes: Placed by one hand-picked point, Grant centre half its width beyond the drawn edge, and a derived second point; low confidence.
The Wellington is drawn again on the main part of the sheet.

Perry, Jackson, Chestnut, Mansion / S. Lafayette, North, Congress, Windsor Av, Grant; Cape Island Creek; 50 ft; two parts: 1 main, 2 boxed corner at the lower right (Grant / S. Lafayette), placed from one hand-picked point.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the beachfront of Cape May City between Jackson Street at the top and Grant Street at the bottom, from South Lafayette and Mansion on the west to the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The upper left corner is a commercial block along Washington and Mansion, with continuous rows of brick and frame stores, offices, a printing works, a candy factory, a plumber, a drug store and a number of boarding houses, some with iron fronts shown in grey. Perry crosses the sheet from left to right above the Congress Hall Hotel, the large pink-coloured hotel with its parlor and guest rooms and dining room, marked closed in the summer of 1908. Between Jackson and Perry, dwellings and the Lansdowne, a bowling alley and a furniture store line the blocks, ending in bath houses at the beach, including Maguires Bath Houses, P. F. Quidort Bath Houses and R. M. Benstead Bath Houses. The Windsor Hotel and the Victoria Boarding stand along Windsor between Congress and Grant, and Public Pavilion No. 3 stands at the foot of the sheet beside the Boardwalk. Beach Avenue runs diagonally along the shore with the Boardwalk drawn beside it, and the ocean fills the lower right. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Adjoining sheets are 14, 15, 9 and 11.
notes: Congress Av. here is Congress Place in OpenStreetMap; Congress is Congress Street.
Boardwalk is printed 'Board walk'; Beach Avenue runs beside it.
Perry / South Lafayette was rejected (13 m): the node 13 m from Mansion / Perry is not the drawn corner; Mansion / Perry fits.
Jackson, Perry, Congress Av (Congress Place today), Congress, Windsor, Grant, S. Lafayette, Mansion, Washington, Beach Av and the boardwalk; Congress Hall; 50 ft.

sheet-13-1.description: Sheet 13 lies on the north-west edge of the built-up part of Cape May City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Cape Island Creek, a broad blue channel, curves across the sheet from the upper centre to the lower left, with a branch drawn in the box at the upper left. East of the creek the W. J. & S. R.R. (Penna R.R.), drawn as several parallel tracks, runs north to south on the sheet to a depot and a freight house at the bottom, with long platforms and sheds. Beside the tracks are the lumber yards of Geo. Ogden and Son, contractors and lumber dealers, with lumber sheds, a sash and door warehouse and a wood working shop, and a gasoline tank is marked underground. The Cape May Light and Power Co., drawn in blue with its engine and dynamo room, stands in the upper middle with a note that a man is on duty at all times. East of Bank, a grid of narrow streets, Bank, Elmira and Broad, with Haynes across the top, holds small frame dwellings, a livery, a wagon shed and a mill on lots of fifty feet and less, while the east side of the sheet is largely open. The lower left corner shows a few dwellings and a tin shop at the junction of Jackson, Chestnut and Perry. A boxed area at the upper left, drawn separately at a different orientation, belongs to West Cape May Borough and is not part of this part. Water pipes of 6 inches are drawn in the streets. Adjoining sheets are 11, 14 and 16.
notes: Haynes is Venice Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The streets here are drawn 27 to 31 ft against 45 ft in the parcels; street_widths set for Bank, Elmira and Broad.
The modern node for Broad / Elmira carries 4.4 m residual.

Cape Island Creek, Penna R.R. depot and lumber yards, Bank, Elmira, Broad, Haynes (Venice Avenue today), Jackson; 50 ft; two parts: 1 main, 2 box at the top left (West Cape May Borough on W. Perry), not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: box at the top left: West Cape May Borough lots on W. Perry (Turnpike), branch of Cape Island Creek (no street junction; own rotation; needs carried points from sheet-11 (W. Perry lots) if the same lots are drawn there).

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the centre of Cape May City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Washington runs across the lower middle of the sheet and is the main business street, lined on both sides with continuous rows of stores, offices, a bank, the post office and the U.S. Weather Bureau, a pool room, a telegraph office and a Y.M.C.A. At the left Jackson holds the Auditorium and a theatre, with hotels and lodging houses including the Homestead, the El Drisco, the Douglass (colored) and the New Cape May Hotel. Ocean, at the lower right, has the Columbia hotel, the Cecil and the Cape May Herald printing office. Lafayette crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally, with St. Mary's Parochial School, St. Mary's R. C. Church and its rectory, the Episcopal Church of the Advent, a chemical engine company, a Macedonia Baptist church and the Baldwin Cottage. In the upper right the Atlantic City Railroad (Reading) enters from the north to a passenger depot and a freight depot beside a long covered platform, with the American Ice and Coal Co. trestle and coal bins, a skating rink and the Cape May Grain Co. beyond. Broad, Bank and Elmira cross the top, with dwellings and a florist's greenhouses. The lower left and lower centre blocks hold dwellings on narrow lots south of Washington down to Hughes. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in all streets. Adjoining sheets are 11, 12, 13, 15, 16 and 17.
notes: Lafayette is Lafayette Street in OpenStreetMap; Washington is Washington Street and, on the pedestrian mall, Washington Mall.
Ocean / Washington was excluded: the detector placed the drawn junction 5 m from the modern node.
Jackson / Lafayette was hand-picked; the detector missed it.
Downtown: Washington, Jackson, Decatur, Ocean, Hughes, Lafayette, Broad, Bank, Elmira, Mansion; Reading depot at the upper right; 50 ft.

sheet-15-1.description: Sheet 15 covers the seafront blocks of Cape May City between Howard and Jackson, from Hughes and Columbia Avenue on the west to the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. In the upper left, a row of dwellings faces Columbia Avenue on both sides, including Griffith Cottage (Boarding) and a drug store at the corner of Ocean. Between Gurney and Ocean, east of Columbia Avenue, are the Colonial Hotel, a row of narrow dwellings and the Stockton Surf Baths with their rows of bath houses at the beach. South of Ocean stand the Star Villa, the Lafayette Hotel and the Aldine, with the First Presbyterian Church, drawn in blue, west of Columbia. Between Decatur and Jackson lie the Baltimore Inn, the Virginia, Carroll Villa, the Merion, Arnold House with its summer garden, and the Shields bath houses, with Public Pavilion No. 2 and the landward end of the Cape May Pier beside the Boardwalk at the lower right. Beach Avenue runs diagonally along the shore with the Boardwalk drawn beside it. Water pipes of 6 inches and hydrants are drawn in all streets and fire alarm boxes stand at Gurney and Decatur. An inset at the top right, outlined with a heavy line, shows the head of the Cape May Pier built on piles, with its theatre, stage and scenery, and a pavilion; it is a separate part and not covered here. Adjoining sheets are 12, 14, 17 and 18.
notes: Columbia Av. is Columbia Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Howard, Hughes, Gurney, Ocean, Decatur and Jackson are Howard Street, Hughes Street, Gurney Street, Ocean Street, Decatur Street and Jackson Street.
The Boardwalk is printed 'Board walk'. The Cape May Pier no longer exists.
Columbia Av, Howard, Hughes, Gurney, Ocean, Decatur, Jackson, Beach Av; Cape May Pier; 50 ft; two parts: 1 main, 2 inset of the pier head (theatre, pavilion) at the top right, not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Cape May Pier head (theatre, stage, pavilion) (the pier no longer exists; no junction; needs a point carried from the pier root on part 1 and the pier axis).

sheet-16-1.description: Sheet 16 covers the north-central part of Cape May City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Lafayette runs nearly across the page. Lafayette crosses the sheet from left to right, with Broad parallel to it above and Washington along the bottom. Franklin runs down the sheet from Lafayette to Washington, and Jefferson closes the right side, with Osborne crossing between them. St. John and Bannaker run up from Lafayette between Franklin and Jefferson. Left of the centre the Atlantic City Railroad (Reading) and the line of the W.J. & S. R.R. (Penna) cross the sheet on a diagonal. The main institutional buildings are Cape May High School between Lafayette and Washington, the Franklin St. M.E. Church, the Public School, the Jail, the Fire Department and City Hall at the foot of Franklin, the 1st Baptist Church and the A.M.E. Church on Franklin and Lafayette, and the 1st M.E. Church and a chapel at the lower left. The Cape May Gas Light Co. works occupies the block on the right between St. John and the sheet edge, with its generator house, purifying house, tar tank, oil tank and gasometers. The Cape May Baking Co. stands on Broad. Above Broad the blocks hold scattered dwellings and large undivided lots, and a street marked No Name runs up beside the railroad. Cape May Golf Grounds lie beyond the right edge. The upper left corner is a boxed area showing the American Ice Co. factory and the railroad, outlined with a heavy line and not part of this part. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches are drawn in the streets.
notes: Lafayette, Franklin, Washington, Jefferson, Broad and Osborne are printed without suffixes; OpenStreetMap has Lafayette Street, Franklin Street, Washington Street, Jefferson Street, Broad Street and Osborne Street.
St. John is Saint Johns Street in OpenStreetMap; north of Broad the drawn street is marked 12 feet wide.
Bannaker and the street marked No Name are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The boxed area at the top left (American Ice Co. Factory No. 2, labelled 24 and 16) is a separate drawing and was left unplaced.
Lafayette, Broad, Franklin, Washington, Jefferson, Osborne, St. John, Bannaker; railroads; gas works; 50 ft; two parts: 1 main, 2 box at the top left (American Ice Co. factory), not placed.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: box at the top left: American Ice Co. factory and the W.J.&S. R.R. (no street junction; needs a point carried from sheet-13 or sheet-24, or a rail crossing).

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 shows a residential and hotel district of Cape May City near the beach front, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Washington runs down the left side and Corgie, Hughes and Columbia Av. follow to its right, all running down the sheet. Jefferson crosses the top, Franklin crosses the middle, and Pearl Av. lies between them east of Corgie. Page and an alley run beside the blocks east of Corgie. Howard crosses the lower right, bending to run diagonally from Columbia Av. to Sewell Av., with a second stretch along the bottom of the block below Hughes. The left side is occupied by large lots, including St. John's Episcopal Church on Washington at Franklin and a church lot with a large garden at the upper left. Townsend's Auto Garage, an iron-clad building, stands on Washington near the bottom. Between Hughes and Columbia lie St. Margaret's Home, hot houses with glass roofs and many frame dwellings, mostly two storeys. On the right, along Columbia Av., stands the Chalfonte Hotel with its laundry and kitchen, and the lawn of the Stockton and a base ball ground fills the lower right corner. Sewell Av. runs up the right edge, with Benton Ave. and Franklin St. lettered beyond it. Water pipes of 6, 8 and 10 inches are drawn in most streets. The adjoining sheets are 16 on the left, 19 above, 15 and 14 below and 18 on the right.
notes: Jefferson, Washington, Corgie, Franklin, Hughes and Howard are printed without suffixes; OpenStreetMap has Jefferson Street, Washington Street, Corgie Street, Franklin Street, Hughes Street and Howard Street.
Pearl Av. is Pearl Street in OpenStreetMap. The street lettered Page and Alley is Page Street in OpenStreetMap.
Franklin / Hughes was hand-picked as a T junction.
Jefferson, Franklin, Washington, Corgie, Hughes, Columbia Av, Pearl Av, Page Alley, Howard, Sewell Av; Chalfonte Hotel; 50 ft.
placenames: The Stockton Lawn and Base Ball Grounds

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the beach-front end of Cape May City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the ocean at the right and the page turned so that Jefferson runs along the top. Kearney Av., Stockton Av. and Beach Av. run down the sheet from Jefferson, with Benton Av. and Franklin at the left edge. Howard and Gurney cross the lower half diagonally from the lower left toward Beach Av., and Columbia Av. runs off the lower left corner with Sewell Ave. at the left edge. Most of the lower half is taken by The Stockton, a large hotel with its dining room, kitchen, laundry, servants quarters, bar room, bowling and billiard rooms, beer garden, office and parlors, platforms and water tanks, and by Stockton Lawn used for base ball field, with a grand stand. Between Jefferson and Howard the blocks hold frame dwellings, several with open porches, and a cottage. East of Beach Av. a Boardwalk, drawn with yellow bands, runs along the shore beside the Atlantic Ocean, and Public Pavilion No. 1 with a reading room stands on the beach at the lower right, 165 feet to the end. Fire alarm boxes are marked on Howard and at the lower left. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in the streets. The adjoining sheets are 20 above, 17 to the left and 15 below.
notes: Jefferson, Franklin, Howard and Gurney are printed without suffixes; OpenStreetMap has Jefferson Street, Franklin Street, Howard Street and Gurney Street.
Kearney Avenue south of Howard is not drawn through the hotel; the Gurney / Kearney junction was left out.
Jefferson, Franklin, Kearney Av, Stockton Av, Benton Av, Beach Av and boardwalk, Howard, Gurney, Columbia Av; The Stockton hotel; 50 ft.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers a residential district in the north-west of Cape May City between Lafayette Street and Corgie, from Madison Avenue at the top to Jefferson at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Washington runs up the middle of the sheet and Queen crosses from Lafayette to Corgie. West of Lafayette lie the grounds of the Cape May Golf Club, left blank. The blocks are mostly given to two-storey frame dwellings on deep lots, with stables and outbuildings behind them. At the top left a large lot marked City Property holds a wagon shed, a store house and a well. Other named buildings are White Hall, the quarters for hotel help at the corner of Lafayette and Jefferson, the Bryan Villa east of Corgie, and Brook's Livery with its wagon sheds and private stables along Jefferson at the lower right. In the upper right corner, on Madison Avenue, stands the Cape May City Sewer Pump House with a gasoline engine. Water pipes of 6 to 16 inches are drawn in all the streets, including a 16 inch main to the water works along Lafayette and Madison Avenue. Osborne Street is lettered where it meets Jefferson at the bottom edge. The adjoining sheets are 16 and 17 below and 22 above; the right-hand edge is unmapped.
notes: Lafayette, Queen, Washington, Corgie and Jefferson are printed without suffixes; OpenStreetMap has Lafayette Street, Queen Street, Washington Street, Corgie Street and Jefferson Street.
Pilot sheet of the atlas: ink_below_paper 100 found all 9 junctions (138 found 7).
Pilot sheet. Lafayette, Queen, Washington, Corgie, Madison Av, Jefferson; Cape May Golf Club grounds; 50 ft.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows the beach-front blocks of Cape May City between Madison Av. and Jefferson, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the ocean at the right and the page turned so that Queen and Jefferson run across it. Benton Av., Kearney Av., Stockton Av. and Beach Av. run down the sheet, and Bullitt Av. crosses the lower left, with Queen crossing the middle. Madison Av. crosses the top as a wide street on a diagonal, with New York Av. and New Jersey Av. entering it from above and Maryland Av. at the upper left. Most of the sheet is vacant, divided into numbered lots with their lot lines drawn, especially the blocks above Queen and those at the left. Frame dwellings of two and a half and three storeys stand along Stockton Av. and Beach Av. in the blocks below Queen, with a fire alarm box on Stockton Av. At the top, a block is marked as the site of the U.S. Life Saving Station. East of Beach Av. the Boardwalk is drawn with yellow bands beside the Atlantic Ocean, and the margin reads Ocean Beyond. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 12 inches are drawn in the streets. The adjoining sheets are 18 below and 19 above.
notes: Queen and Jefferson are printed without suffixes; OpenStreetMap has Queen Street and Jefferson Street.
Bullitt Av. is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The sheet says U.S. Life Saving Station on this block at the top.
Madison Av, New York, New Jersey, Maryland, Queen, Bullitt Av, Benton, Kearney, Stockton, Beach Av, Jefferson; mostly vacant lots; 50 ft.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the north-west edge of Cape May City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Lafayette and Washington run down the sheet side by side, and Union joins them near the middle. West crosses the upper part east of Washington, and Cake runs east from Washington near the bottom. At the upper right Massachusetts Av. runs down the sheet, with Reading Av. and Vermont Av. entering from the upper right corner and enclosing a triangular block. The upper right is cut into narrow numbered lots, laid out in rows with their lot lines but without buildings. Along Washington and Lafayette the blocks hold two-storey frame dwellings, with a tin shop at the lower centre. West of Lafayette lies land of the Cape May Golf Links, left blank, with three lots and a few dwellings in the lower left. At the top of the sheet stand a large house and outbuildings on Lafayette. A fire alarm box stands on Washington near the middle. Water pipes of 6 inches are drawn along Washington. The right half of the sheet below West is unmapped. The adjoining sheets are 23 above and 22 below.
notes: Lafayette, Washington, Union, West and Cake are printed without suffixes; OpenStreetMap has Lafayette Street, Washington Street, Union Street, West Street and Cake Street.
Massachusetts / Vermont was not detected and is not used.
Washington / Cake was hand-picked (Cake is 20 feet wide).
Lafayette, Washington, Union, West, Cake, Massachusetts, Vermont, Reading Avs; 50 ft.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the northern edge of the built-up area of Cape May City, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Lafayette and Washington run down the sheet, converging slightly toward the top, and Schellenger crosses between them in the upper part. Madison Av. crosses the foot of the sheet on a diagonal, joining Lafayette at the lower left and Washington at the bottom. West of Lafayette are the grounds of the Cape May Golf Club, with a club house and a buffet building at the left, and above them the margin reads Golf Links Beyond. Between Lafayette and Washington the blocks hold two-storey frame dwellings, with long vacant lots in the middle. East of Washington stands a large lot with a house, several outbuildings and a hot house with glass roof, and farther south a hot house and a few dwellings and a row of houses on the right of Washington near Madison Av. Water pipes of 6 inches run in Lafayette and Washington, and 16 inch pipes run along Madison Av. Lots are numbered and lettered buildings A, B and C stand on the large lot. A fire alarm box stands at Madison Av. and Washington. The adjoining sheets are 21 above and 19 below.
notes: Lafayette, Washington and Schellenger are printed without suffixes; OpenStreetMap has Lafayette Street and Washington Street.
The street printed Schellenger is Schellenger Landing Road in OpenStreetMap here; the OpenStreetMap Schellenger Street lies about a kilometre farther north.
Only 4 control points: low to medium confidence.
Lafayette, Washington, Schellenger (Schellenger Landing Road today), Madison Av; golf club; 50 ft; four junctions only.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the north-eastern edge of Cape May City toward Schellenger's Landing, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Lafayette Street and Washington Street run up the sheet side by side, with Sidney Avenue crossing between them near the top; Texas Avenue curves across the top toward the harbour, and on the right Massachusetts Avenue is met by Trenton, Wisconsin, Reading and Vermont Avenues coming in on the diagonal from the east. The blocks between Lafayette and Washington Streets are residential, with scattered frame dwellings, sheds and a small shop, while west of Lafayette Street lie large lots with a few dwellings and a boat builder's shop. Between Washington Street and Massachusetts Avenue two long blocks are subdivided into narrow numbered lots that are almost all vacant, apart from one building near Texas Avenue; the triangular blocks east of Massachusetts Avenue are likewise laid out in lots without buildings. A 6 inch water pipe runs in Washington Street. The sheet joins sheet 24 at the top, where Lafayette and Washington Streets continue toward the harbour, and sheet 21 at the bottom. Large parts of the sheet are open, undeveloped ground, reflecting the edge of the built-up town in 1909.
notes: Lafayette and Washington are printed without a suffix; they are Lafayette Street and Washington Street today.
The unlabelled 60 ft street between Washington Street and Massachusetts Avenue is East Street in OpenStreetMap.
Texas Avenue / Washington Street was not used: OpenStreetMap has two nodes there about 37 m apart, neither matching the drawn junction well.
Lafayette, Washington, Sidney Av, Texas Av, Massachusetts Av, Trenton, Wisconsin, Reading, Vermont Avs; 50 ft.

sheet-24-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 24 shows the harbour front of Cape May City at Schellenger's Landing on Cape Island Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Along the left edge Lafayette and Washington Streets come in from sheet 23; Lafayette Street crosses the creek on a bridge, and Texas Avenue curves down to the water past the end of Massachusetts Avenue. Between Lafayette and Washington Streets stand a few dwellings, an octagonal house, a machine shop, a gasoline tank and the Cape May Yacht Club with its bar. The rest of the part is water and shore: the dredged basin of Schellenger's Landing, the wide channel of Cape Island Creek and the inlet called Devil's Reach, lined with boat houses, sheds, a carpenter's shop, a paint shop and a club house. A row of boat houses on the north bank of the creek carries the names of their owners. On the marsh at the lower right a cluster of boat houses and small cottages, several of them named, is reached by plank walks drawn as dashed lines. Much of the marsh and the open ground south of Texas Avenue is blank. An inset in the upper right corner, divided off by a heavy line, shows more boat houses along Cape Island Creek and is a separate part.
notes: Placed from one feature carried from sheet 23 (the octagonal dwelling between Lafayette and Washington Streets) and a derived point along Washington Street; scale and rotation are assumed, not measured. Low confidence away from the left edge.
Schellenger's Landing and the harbour have been dredged and rebuilt since 1909; the drawn shoreline should not be expected to match the modern one.
Lafayette and Washington are printed without a suffix (Lafayette Street, Washington Street today).

Schellenger's Landing and Cape Island Creek harbour, 50 ft, two parts: 1 main (Lafayette, Washington, Texas Av, yacht club, boat houses; placed from a building carried from sheet 23 and a derived point), 2 inset at the top right of boat houses along Cape Island Creek (not placed).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: boat houses along Cape Island Creek, upper right (no street junction; harbour shoreline rebuilt).

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the eastern end of Cape May City, a newly laid-out seaside subdivision east of the built-up town, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the left of the page. Long narrow blocks run between Cape May Avenue on the west and Beach Avenue and the boardwalk along the Atlantic Ocean on the east, cut by Idaho, Maryland, New York and New Jersey Avenues, and crossed by Brooklyn, Baltimore, Pittsburg and Trenton Avenues. Cape May Avenue is drawn as a boulevard about 200 feet wide with a planted median, and Pittsburg Avenue is 100 feet wide. Nearly every block is divided into numbered lots of about 25 feet frontage, but almost all of them are vacant: only a handful of frame dwellings stand near Beach Avenue at the ocean end of the blocks. The one large building is the Hotel Cape May, a fireproof hotel occupying the whole block between Baltimore and Pittsburg Avenues on the ocean front, with a printed note describing its night watchman, standpipes, pumps and laundry, and a tennis court beside it. The boardwalk runs along the ocean side of Beach Avenue, with the shoreline of the Atlantic beyond it. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are drawn in Baltimore, Pittsburg and New Jersey Avenues. The block numbers run from 1 to 21 across the sheet. The adjoining blocks along the sheet edges are not mapped on other sheets of this atlas.
notes: Hotel Cape May, fireproof construction, occupies the ocean-front block between Baltimore and Pittsburg Avenues.
Cape May Avenue is drawn with a 200 ft planted median; OpenStreetMap maps it as two roadways about 40 m apart, so it was left out of the control.
Beach Avenue has the boardwalk on its ocean side and was not detected; control comes from the interior avenues.
East end of Cape May City: Cape May Av to Beach Av, Brooklyn to Trenton Av; Hotel Cape May; 100 ft to an inch, north to the left.
